paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is about. These brothers walk into Egypt thinking they're just buying grain. But the real thing on the table is what they did to Joseph years ago. They never dealt with it, and it comes up the second they're under pressure (Genesis 42:21).

Look at what they say to one another: "Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen." (Genesis 42:21). They had never stopped carrying it. And Reuben says, "Now we must account for his blood!" (Genesis 42:22). I think that tells us something true, baker: a thing you bury doesn't leave. It just waits for a quiet moment.

But look who else is in this passage. Joseph recognizes them, and I think he turns away and weeps because it still matters to him (Genesis 42:24). And he says, "I fear God" (Genesis 42:18). So the story isn't only about guilt. It's about a God who is working while people are afraid and confused, and the story isn't over. So if something is heavy on your heart today, baker, bring it into the light now, because carrying it alone is a LOT heavier than I ever carried those cookie boxes.
